paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: in the family of God, we don't get to be each other's judge. Paul says the one who eats everything must not belittle the one who doesn't, and the one who doesn't must not judge the one who does, "for God has accepted him" (Romans 14:3). Nobody gets to climb up on a high stool and grade somebody else's cookies. Each of us stands or falls before our own Master, and Paul says the Lord is able to make His servant stand (Romans 14:4).

Why does that matter? Because "none of us lives to himself alone," and "whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord" (Romans 14:7-8). Christ died and returned to life to be Lord of both the dead and the living (Romans 14:9), so He's the Lord of the baker next to you too. And so, Paul says, "each of us will give an account of himself to God" (Romans 14:12). I'll be honest, friend, I've got enough to explain about my OWN batches without taking on yours!

So what do we do with that? We stop judging, and we choose love. If a brother is distressed by what you eat, you are "no longer acting in love," because he's someone Christ died for (Romans 14:15). The kingdom of God is "righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit" (Romans 14:17), so go after what leads to peace and to building each other up (Romans 14:19). Keep your own convictions between you and God, and live every bit of it from faith.
